bib.title: d1: Scaling Reasoning in Diffusion Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning

question: Can masked diffusion LLMs be turned into stronger reasoning models with SFT and online policy-gradient RL, given that GRPO needs log-probabilities dLLMs cannot compute cheaply?
hypothesis: Combining masked SFT on reasoning traces with a GRPO variant using a one-step log-prob estimator improves dLLM reasoning more than either alone.
contributions: d1, a two-stage SFT + RL framework for masked dLLMs
diffu-GRPO: GRPO with mean-field sequence log-prob and one-step per-token log-prob estimation with random prompt masking, first policy-gradient RL on masked dLLMs
Empirical study on math, planning and coding showing d1 gives the best results
Ablations on random masking, mu and p_mask

method.summary: Starting from LLaDA-8B-Instruct, SFT on s1k with masked-diffusion loss, then diffu-GRPO per task using a one-step log-probability estimator with randomly masked prompts so many inner gradient updates can reuse one batch of generations. Evaluated zero-shot at generation lengths 128/256/512.
method.task: reasoning post-training of diffusion LLMs (math, planning, coding)

datasets.name: s1K
datasets.split: 1% held out for evaluation; truncated to max 4096 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: truncated to 4096 tokens; padded to model max length so PAD tokens enter the loss

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: train split for RL, test split for eval

datasets.name: MATH500 / MATH
datasets.split: train split of MATH for RL (ankner/math-500)

datasets.name: Countdown (3 numbers)
datasets.split: train from TinyZero Countdown-Tasks-3to4 restricted to 3 numbers

datasets.name: 4x4 Sudoku
datasets.size: train subset of one million unique puzzles; eval 256 randomly generated puzzles

models.name: LLaDA-8B-Instruct
models.context: inferred: pre-trained on sequences up to 4096 tokens (Sec 4.3)

training.objective: diffu-GRPO: clipped GRPO objective with unnormalised advantage A=r-mean(r), reverse KL, using one-step per-token log-prob estimate with prompt masking and mean-field sequence log-prob; SFT: masked-diffusion NELBO weighted 1/t on masked response tokens
training.optimizer: AdamW, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99 (RL); SFT optimizer and schedule 'match' RL
training.lr_schedule: SFT: linear decay; RL: not stated
training.batch_size: RL: 6 per GPU x 8 GPUs x grad accum 2; coding: 2 per device x 4 GPUs x grad accum 4; SFT: per-device 1, grad accum 4, effective 8
training.steps: diffu-GRPO: 7700 GSM8K, 6600 MATH500, 5000 Countdown, 3800 Sudoku; coding 7500 (base) and 9000 (SFT start); SFT 2460 steps
training.regularisation: gradient clipping 0.2 (RL), 1.0 (SFT); KL beta and clip eps not stated in text; random prompt masking
training.hardware: RL: 8x NVIDIA A100-80G; coding RL: 4x RTX A5000; SFT: 2x A6000
training.wall_clock: Fig 5 shows up to about 20 hours on GSM8K ablation (read from Fig 5)

other.mu_main_runs: not stated for main runs; ablation uses mu=12 (Fig 5 compares mu of 2, 12 and 24)
other.eval_checkpoint: RL models evaluated every 100 steps from step 600, best reported (selection on eval)

inference.decoding: semi-autoregressive block decoding: blocks of 32 tokens, N/2 denoising steps, unmask 2 highest-confidence tokens per step within block; greedy
inference.samples: single greedy run per setting; no seeds reported

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct on each benchmark (Sudoku/Countdown test sets of 256 generated instances)

metrics.name: effective tokens
metrics.definition: average number of non-padding, non-EOS tokens per generation

eval.protocol: 0-shot, greedy, three generation lengths; best checkpoint chosen from evaluation for RL models; no seeds or significance tests

results.claim: d1-LLaDA (SFT then diffu-GRPO) reaches 82.1 on GSM8K at generation length 512, vs 78.2 for base LLaDA-8B-Instruct
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct base, zero-shot, greedy decoding; per-task diffu-GRPO trained with online generation length 256; best checkpoint among steps 600,700,... reported for RL models
results.table: Table 1, row + SFT + diffu-GRPO (d1-LLaDA), column GSM8K 512

results.claim: d1-LLaDA reaches 40.2 on MATH500 at length 512 vs 36.2 base
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct base, zero-shot, greedy decoding; per-task diffu-GRPO trained with online generation length 256; best checkpoint among steps 600,700,... reported for RL models

results.claim: d1-LLaDA reaches 42.2 on Countdown at length 512 vs 16.0 for base at the same length (base best is 20.7 at 128)
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct base, zero-shot, greedy decoding; per-task diffu-GRPO trained with online generation length 256; best checkpoint among steps 600,700,... reported for RL models

results.claim: d1-LLaDA reaches 22.1 on 4x4 Sudoku at length 128 vs 11.7 base
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct base, zero-shot, greedy decoding; per-task diffu-GRPO trained with online generation length 256; best checkpoint among steps 600,700,... reported for RL models

results.claim: Reported gains of d1-LLaDA over base: modest on math, larger on planning
results.note: Paper does not say which lengths are compared. 3.9 and 4.0 match best-length differences (82.1-78.2, 40.2-36.2); 26.2 matches 42.2-16.0 at length 512; Sudoku 10.0 does not match 22.1-11.7=10.4 exactly. Not reconciled by the authors.
results.quote: we observe modest improvements on GSM8K (3.9%) and MATH500 (4.0%), but significantly larger gains on Countdown (26.2%) and Sudoku (10.0%)

results.claim: diffu-GRPO beats base LLaDA and SFT in all 12 setups; SFT beats base in only 7 of 12
results.quote: diffu-GRPO outperforms both LLaDA-8B-Instruct and SFT, in all 12 setups, while SFT outperforms LLaDA-8B-Instruct in only 7 of

results.claim: d1 (SFT + diffu-GRPO) outperforms diffu-GRPO alone in 11 of 12 setups
results.quote: This combined approach outperforms pure diffu-GRPO in 11 out of 12 setups

results.claim: diffu-GRPO alone on Countdown: 37.1 at 512 vs 16.0 base and 23.8 SFT
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct base, zero-shot, greedy decoding; per-task diffu-GRPO trained with online generation length 256; best checkpoint among steps 600,700,... reported for RL models

results.claim: A single unified diffu-GRPO model across four tasks keeps accuracy close to per-task models (combined d1-LLaDA GSM8K 75.1 at length 128)
results.setup: One model trained on combined GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, Sudoku with data subsampled to equal size per task; lengths 128 and 256 only
results.note: Combined model is not uniformly better than per-task: e.g. combined d1-LLaDA Sudoku 21.9 at 128 vs 22.1 per-task; MATH500 29.8 vs 33.8.
results.table: Table 2, row combined d1-LLaDA, column GSM8K 128

results.claim: diffu-GRPO on KodCode-Light-RL-10K improves HumanEval at length 256 from 35.3 to 39.0 on the base model
results.setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct trained with diffu-GRPO on KodCode-Light-RL-10K; HumanEval 164 problems
results.note: Not uniform: base+diffu-GRPO drops 3.0 on HumanEval at 512 (37.8 to 34.8).

results.claim: On top of the s1k SFT checkpoint, diffu-GRPO gives +9.8 on HumanEval at length 128
results.table: Table 3, row Delta (diffu-GRPO gain) under SFT, column HumanEval 128

results.claim: Random prompt masking lets the number of inner updates mu scale to 12 or 24 while conventional practice caps mu at 2; higher mu reaches same reward in less wall-clock time
results.setup: GSM8K correctness reward vs completions generated, fixed vs random masking, mu in {2,12,24}; read from Fig 5, no numeric wall-clock reported in text
results.quote: While conventional approaches typically limit µ to 2 due to diminishing returns and overfitting risks, our approach enables scaling µ to much higher values (12, or even 24)

results.claim: Prompt masking probability: 0.1 and 0.3 are stable, 0.5 and 0.7 unstable, 0.7 degrades sharply after 3000 steps, 0.0 slightly underperforms
results.quote: with 0.7 causing sharp degradation after 3000 steps

results.claim: d1-LLaDA gets highest GSM8K and second-highest MATH500 among dLLMs and AR LLMs of similar size
results.setup: Comparison with Dream 7B, Qwen2.5 7B, LLaMA3 8B, Mistral 7B, Deepseek 7B; other-model scores copied from Dream with 8-shot GSM8K, 4-shot MATH, while LLaDA/d1 are 0-shot task-specific RL, so not like-for-like
results.quote: d1-LLaDA achieves the highest GSM8K score and the second-highest MATH500 score

results.claim: Going from generation length 128 to 256 improves math more than 256 to 512
results.setup: GSM8K and MATH500, all four models
results.quote: larger jumps observed from 128 to 256 (∼7.1%), than from 256 to 512 (∼2.5%)

results.claim: Sudoku accuracy falls with longer generation for all models; Countdown base falls monotonically while SFT/RL variants peak at 512
results.quote: Performance decreases with increasing sequence lengths for Sudoku across all models.

results.claim: No significant chain-of-thought length growth after RL, unlike DeepSeek-R1
results.quote: we observe no significant CoT length growth post-RL training, as LLaDA-8B-Instruct was pre-trained on sequences up to 4096 tokens

results.claim: Aha moments (self-verification, backtracking) appear qualitatively at length 512 in SFT and d1-LLaDA outputs only
results.setup: GSM8K examples, Appendix E; anecdotal, a few samples
results.quote: at sequence length 512, we begin observing “aha moments” in the SFT and d1-LLaDA models

limits: Authors: fixed-length generation in LLaDA means diffu-GRPO trains at a predefined length (256), may prevent finding concise or long CoT; suggest Block Diffusion
Online generation speed limits RL generation length; scaling length infeasible now
s1k not suitable for coding as it lacks code
Per-task RL models; best checkpoint selected on evaluation; single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals
Gains on Sudoku shrink at longer lengths; Table 3 shows some negative gains
Mean-field and one-step log-prob estimates are heuristics with no bias analysis; KL beta, clip epsilon, G and main-run mu not stated
Qualitative aha-moment evidence is a few examples
